description: Declarative tool-call policy for the open pack. Edit this file to change enforcement without touching JS. severity: warn (log + console.warn, never blocks) | ask (native permission.ask prompt, degrades to warn if the event does not fire for bash) | deny (throws in tool.execute.before, blocks the call). Default is conservative: only catastrophic/irreversible operations are deny.

rules.message: rm -rf on an absolute path can destroy the OS or the whole workspace irreversibly.
rm -rf on the home directory is irreversible.
rm -rf on a parent directory; confirm the target before continuing.
Overwriting a raw block device destroys the disk irreversibly.
mkfs formats a filesystem and destroys its contents irreversibly.
dd writing to a raw device destroys the target irreversibly.
Fork bomb; it will exhaust the machine.
git push --force can rewrite shared remote history irreversibly.
git push -f can rewrite shared remote history irreversibly.
git reset --hard discards local changes; recoverable via reflog if caught early.
git clean -fd deletes untracked files; confirm the target.
git branch -D force-deletes a branch even if unmerged.
git update-ref -d deletes a ref directly; confirm the target.
DROP DATABASE/SCHEMA destroys the whole schema irreversibly.
DROP TABLE is legitimate in migrations; warn, do not block.
TRUNCATE removes all rows; legitimate in migrations, warn only.
DELETE FROM without WHERE deletes every row; confirm before running.
shutdown stops the machine; confirm it is intended.
reboot restarts the machine; confirm it is intended.
halt powers off the machine; confirm it is intended.
